headline: Futures jumped overnight (S&P 500 +1.76% to 7,322.50, Nasdaq-100 +2.55%, Dow +537 pts) as battered AI chip stocks rebounded and China's stocks surged on Beijing support pledges, while oil rose on Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites; a Dec 9 Fed hike stays about 99% priced.
regime: Hiking regime with a sharp holiday rebound: the Fed funds target is 3.75-4.00%, a 25bp hike on Dec 9 is 98.9% priced (CME FedWatch via Forbes), the 10-year is about 4.84%, the VIX has eased to about 25.6 and the Nasdaq-100 is still down about 8% for November.

lean.why: S&P 500 futures were up about 1.7-1.9% and Nasdaq-100 futures 2.4-2.6% before the open; AI hardware names averaged +5.8% premarket (TECHi). The session ends at 1pm ET, so volume is usually thin.
A Dec 9 hike is about 99% priced after core PCE hit 3.3%; the jobs report (Dec 4), FOMC (Dec 9) and CPI (Dec 10) follow, and Section 301 tariff proposals are pending.
Q3 GDP grew 4.3%, but a hiking Fed and a 10-year near 4.84% pressure valuations; the Nasdaq-100 is on track for its worst month since December 2022 (Forbes).

rates.n: Williams says inflation remains too high (Schwab, Nov 25); Waller said in mid-November a 50bp hike might be necessary if inflation does not improve; next FOMC Dec 8-9
CME FedWatch 98.9% for a 25bp hike (Forbes, Nov 27); Reuters cites 99%
Fell to 4.84% early Nov 27 (Yahoo Finance); 4.85% at the Nov 25 close; 2-year and 30-year Treasury levels from Nov 25 (older): 4.61% and 5.24%
Freddie Mac survey released Wed Nov 25 (early for Thanksgiving), down from 7.28%; 15-year 6.54%; year ago 6.23%
103.71 on Nov 25 (older, Capp Notes); Oninvest says the dollar is near its longest winning streak since 2024
Up about 2.5% above $3,670 (Stocktwits, Nov 27); futures $3,700.10, +3.8% in Yahoo's quote bar
WTI $85.80 (+2.60%) and Brent $97.27 (+0.72%) at 5:41am ET Nov 27 (TipRanks), after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure (Yahoo Finance); OPEC+ meets Nov 29
25.58, -4.55%, in Yahoo Finance's quote bar early Nov 27; 28.29 at the Nov 25 close

sectors.why: Premarket Nov 27: AI hardware averaged +5.8% (Nvidia +4.2%, Micron +7.0%, Marvell +8.0%); the proposed tariffs excluded chips and servers. Nvidia is still more than 37% below its October record.
Nutanix -15.19% on a CEO transition, Oracle -5.13%; tech was the worst sector (-0.83%). Salesforce and Snowflake report Dec 2.
Financials +0.71% on Nov 25; a December hike (97.8%) supports lending margins.
30-year mortgage fell to 7.21% from 7.28%; Oct new home sales rose to a 701K annual rate; Dream Finders +9.24%, real estate +0.92%.
Gold rose about 2.5% above $3,670 and silver 7% above $44 on Nov 27 (Stocktwits), recovering from a dip below $3,500 on Nov 25.
WTI $85.80 (+2.60%) and Brent $97.27 on Nov 27 after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites; Kinetik +7% on a Targa takeover report. OPEC+ meets Nov 29.
Adobe: $82.5B online Nov 1-22 (+9.1%), Black Friday seen at $12.9B; NRF sees $1T+ season (+4.2%); Target comps +5.6%. Amazon fell 3.1% Wednesday.
Health care -0.56% on Nov 25; Vertex -7.26% after hours after the FDA pushed its povetacicept decision to Feb 28, 2027.
Russell 2000 futures +1.27% to 2,740.60 Nov 27; the index rose 0.71% to 2,704.06 on Nov 25 and is up 4.7% this week.
Utilities +0.48% as the 10-year fell 6bp to 4.85%; AES leaves the S&P 500 on Dec 2.
Deere +4.44% despite an EPS miss, CNH +8.00%; industrials +0.83%, materials +2.07% (best sector).
WTI near $86 and Brent near $97 on Nov 27 raise fuel costs.

news.head: Stock futures surge into the half-day session; S&P futures top 7,300
news.mean: Dec S&P 500 futures were 7,322.50 (+1.76%), Nasdaq-100 futures 26,766.50 (+2.55%), Dow futures 50,765 (+537 pts) and Russell 2000 futures +1.27% late Thursday. Through Wednesday the S&P 500 was up 3.9% for the week but down 5.24% for November.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: gains in a thin post-holiday half day can be exaggerated and often get tested in the next full session.
news.today: Stocks open 9:30am and close 1pm ET; watch whether the gap holds into the early close.
news.later: A rebound inside a down month does not change the hiking backdrop; the Dec 4 jobs report and Dec 9 FOMC matter more.

news.head: AI hardware rebounds premarket: Nvidia +4.2%, Micron +7%, Marvell +8%
news.mean: Ten AI hardware stocks averaged +5.8% premarket: Nvidia $155.52 (+4.2%), AMD +5.3%, Micron +7.0%, Marvell +8.0%, Dell +5.9%, CoreWeave +7.4%. Forbes had Sandisk +10.8% and Anthropic +3.6% to $85.73, back above its $83 IPO price. The proposed tariffs excluded servers, chips and chipmaking tools.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sharp rebounds after a month-long slide often meet selling near prior breakdown levels.
news.today: Watch whether chip leaders hold their premarket gains after the open.
news.later: Nvidia is still more than 37% below its October record and faces an S&P credit review; Marvell (Dec 1) is the next AI earnings test.

news.head: China stocks soar as Beijing pledges market support; CSI 300 +4.2%
news.mean: The CSI 300 rose 4.2%, its biggest gain since October 2024; the STAR 50 jumped 15%, the Shanghai Composite 3.7% and the Hang Seng 2.1% after the State Council backed 'national team' buying and promised more stimulus. Pepperstone noted no funding commitments or timelines.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: policy-pledge rallies without funding details often fade unless concrete measures follow.
news.today: China-linked ADRs may gap up at the open.
news.later: Watch for actual funding amounts; industrial profits rose 16% y/y through October.

news.head: Oil climbs after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites; WTI near $86
news.mean: WTI was $85.80 (+2.60%) and Brent $97.27 (+0.72%) at 5:41am ET. Yahoo Finance tied the gains to Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. OPEC+ meets Nov 29.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: supply-attack spikes in oil often fade within days unless output is actually lost.
news.today: Energy names may open firm; airlines could lag.
news.later: Sustained $85+ WTI would feed into inflation data the Fed is watching.

news.head: Bitcoin tops $61K, silver +7%, gold back above $3,670
news.mean: Bitcoin rose 1.6% to about $61,600 with $240M of liquidations (71.4% shorts); Strategy rose over 6% premarket and miners 6%+. Silver jumped 7% above $44 and gold 2.5% above $3,670.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: short-squeeze driven crypto moves can reverse quickly if key levels (here $62K, per analysts quoted) are not reclaimed.
news.later: Gold's rebound comes despite a firm dollar and a hiking Fed.

news.head: December hike odds near 99% as futures rally
news.srcN: Forbes, Nov 27; Reuters via MIX-FM, Nov 27
news.mean: CME FedWatch put a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting at 98.9% (Forbes); Reuters cited 99% after Q3 growth was revised up and October inflation accelerated. XTB's Kathleen Brooks said the recovery in stocks 'seems technical'.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: when a move is fully priced, the statement and dot plot usually drive the reaction more than the decision itself.
news.today: Rate-sensitive groups may react to yields rather than equity futures.
news.later: The Dec 4 jobs report and Dec 10 CPI shape whether more hikes follow in 2027.

news.head: Kinetik jumps 7% on report Targa is in talks to buy it
news.mean: Bloomberg reported Targa Resources is in talks to acquire Kinetik at about an $8.9B market value, possibly as soon as next week; Kinetik rose 7% and Targa fell 2-3%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: targets of reported talks often trade below the eventual offer until terms are confirmed; acquirers often dip on announcement.
news.today: Watch for a confirmation or denial.

news.head: Trump calls revised Q3 GDP 'FAKE' and calls for an investigation
news.srcN: Yahoo Finance live blog (citing Bloomberg), Nov 27
news.mean: President Trump posted that the revised Q3 GDP figure of 4.3% was 'FAKE' and called for an investigation, per Bloomberg as reported by Yahoo Finance.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: political criticism of data agencies rarely moves markets on the day but can raise uncertainty around future releases.
news.today: Unlikely to drive the half-day session.
news.later: Watch whether it affects confidence in upcoming jobs and CPI releases.

news.head: Black Friday: Adobe tallies $82.5B online Nov 1-22 (+9.1%); NRF sees $1T+ season
news.mean: Adobe says US online spending reached $82.5B from Nov 1-22 (+9.1% y/y) and expects $12.9B on Black Friday (+9.2%) and 6.7% season growth. NRF expects holiday sales above $1 trillion (+4.2%); Mastercard forecasts +5.5% retail sales Nov 1-Dec 24. Target's Q3 comparable sales rose 5.6%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: early Black Friday tallies get headlines but full-season results matter more for retailers.
news.today: Early in-store and online tallies may move retailers.
news.later: Cyber Monday (Nov 30) is the next data point.

news.head: Palo Alto Networks slides after hours on an ex-employee lawsuit
news.srcN: Stocktwits via Yahoo Finance, Nov 25; Oninvest, Nov 27
news.mean: A former regional VP sued, alleging he was fired for objecting to counting reseller orders as sales; Oninvest said the stock fell 4% after hours and the company denies the claims. PANW closed at $356.14 on Nov 25.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: lawsuit-driven drops often recover unless regulators or auditors follow up.
news.today: Watch whether PANW lags the tech rebound.
news.later: Any auditor or SEC follow-up would matter more than the suit itself.

news.head: Nasdaq dives 4.6% intraday, then pares loss to 0.6%; Dow rises
news.srcN: Reuters via Investing.com, Nov 25; Capp Notes, Nov 25
news.mean: The Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95, the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq fell 0.62% to 23,585.80 after falling as much as 4.6%; the Nasdaq-100 briefly sat 20% below its record close. Reuters cited AI worries centered on Nvidia, new tariff proposals and rising inflation and oil. The Nasdaq is down 7.3% for November; the Russell 2000 rose 0.71%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a large intraday drop that is mostly recovered by the close shows dip buying, but it does not by itself mark a bottom.
news.today: Markets are closed; Friday's half-day may test whether Wednesday's recovery holds.
news.later: Investors may watch whether the Nasdaq-100 closes 20% below its record, a common bear-market definition.

news.head: October PCE inflation rises to 3.8%; core 3.3%, above forecasts
news.srcN: Trend & Ticker, Nov 25; Capp Notes, Nov 25
news.mean: Headline PCE rose 0.3% m/m and 3.8% y/y; core rose 0.3% m/m and 3.3% y/y versus a 3.2% consensus (Capp Notes). Personal income jumped 0.7% (partly one-time Medicare rebates), spending rose 0.3% with real spending flat, and the saving rate was 4.1%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a core PCE reading above forecast usually firms up hike bets, but yields can still fall if growth or risk worries dominate the day.
news.today: No trading today; the next inflation read is November CPI on Dec 10.
news.later: Investors may watch whether core inflation keeps rising from 3.1% in September to 3.3% and beyond.

news.head: Q3 GDP revised up to 4.3% from 3.4%
news.mean: Real GDP grew at a 4.3% annualized rate in the second estimate, up from 3.4% and above the 3.5% expected (Schwab). Final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 5.8%, and corporate profits rose $206.0B versus $384.0B in Q2.
news.hist: Q2 growth was 2.2%, so the revised Q3 figure is about twice as fast.
news.today: Strong growth plus 3.3% core inflation strengthens the case for a hike.
news.later: Schwab notes the revision adds weight to the debate over extending hikes into early 2027.

news.head: US proposes new Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners
news.srcN: Global Trade & Sanctions Law, Nov 25; Stock Titan, Nov 25
news.mean: USTR proposed tariffs over structural excess capacity: up to 20% on most Chinese goods (40% fallback), 15% net of MFN for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan, 18% for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, and up to 35% for Vietnam and 25% for India if no deal. No effective date is set; comments are due Jan 5, 2027 and hearings start Jan 25.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: proposed tariffs with long comment periods often move markets less than final tariffs, and rates can change in negotiations.
news.today: Watch for trading partners' responses over the holiday.
news.later: Investors may watch the Jan 5 comment deadline and the Jan 10 expiry of the US-China truce.

news.head: Nvidia falls 3.9% as S&P warns of a possible credit downgrade
news.srcN: Stock Titan, Nov 25; AP via BNN Bloomberg, Nov 26
news.mean: Nvidia closed down 3.91% after a 31.48% jump Monday and a fall Tuesday. S&P Global Ratings put its rating on watch for a possible cut, citing management and governance concerns after Jensen Huang's reinstatement. Micron fell 4.53%, AMD 1.75%; Lam Research was down 11.64% at 11am and closed -5.68% (Capp Notes).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: credit-rating watches on mega-cap issuers rarely change funding costs much right away, but they can keep governance headlines in focus.
news.today: Asian AI stocks rebounded Thursday; Nvidia rose in late trading Wednesday (no figure given).
news.later: Investors may watch for S&P's final rating decision and the reported Dec 1 House interview with Huang.

calendar.t: Black Friday: stocks close 1pm ET, bonds 2pm; advance goods trade balance and retail/wholesale inventories (8:30am); BridgeBio FDA decision (BBP-418)
calendar.usual: Thin holiday volume; early shopping tallies drive retail headlines; binary move in BBIO.
Output decisions move crude and energy stocks at Monday's open.
Online sales tallies move e-commerce and retail names.

calendar.t: ISM manufacturing PMI (Nov) and JOLTS (Oct, 10am ET); Marvell and Okta earnings (after the close); House interview with Nvidia CEO reported
calendar.usual: Strong data supports the hike case; Marvell reads through to AI chips.

calendar.t: ADP employment (Nov); BMO (before the open); Salesforce, Snowflake, Five Below (after the close); SharkNinja replaces AES in the S&P 500
calendar.usual: ADP previews Friday's jobs report; Salesforce is a software sentiment check.
Usually a small mover unless far from about 200K.
A strong report raises 50bp odds; a weak one eases them.

calendar.t: Q3 productivity and costs, revised (8:30am ET); FOMC meeting begins
calendar.usual: Unit labor costs feed the inflation debate.
A 25bp hike is about 98% priced, so guidance drives the reaction.
First inflation read after the decision; a hot print raises early-2027 hike bets.

scen.title: What if November payrolls (Dec 4, 8:30am ET) are... (October was +165K with 4.1% unemployment; consensus not yet confirmed)

opts.l: Hot (payrolls well above October's +165K, unemployment at or below 4.1%)
In line (payrolls near October's pace, unemployment near 4.1%)
Cold (payrolls well below +165K or unemployment rising above 4.1%)

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Energy stocks win. Airlines, cruise lines and shippers lose. Headline inflation rises, adding to hike pressure.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
